original_question: If A is a Borel subset of [0, infinity) containing 0, does there exist a Borel subset B of the real line whose center of distances C(B) is exactly A?
target_in_paper: Problem 33 in Section 7 ("Center of distances"): the Borel realization problem for centers of distances. It is introduced immediately after Theorem 15, which gives the unrestricted existence result but leaves descriptive-set-theoretic control open. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It has the right ambient target class (Borel subsets of [0, infinity) containing 0), the right witness class (Borel subsets of the real line), and the exact equality requirement C(B)=A. This is essentially Problem 33 verbatim. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, the draft should define the center of distances. In Section 7, for a subset X of a metric space, C(X) is defined as the set of all α≥0 such that for every x∈X there exists y∈X with d(x,y)=α; on the real line this is d(x,y)=|x-y|. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))

The ambient metric should be made explicit: the paper is working with subsets of R equipped with the usual Euclidean metric, and C depends on that metric. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))

If one wants the question to be completely self-contained, one should clarify that the given set A is Borel in the usual topology on [0, infinity) (equivalently, a Borel subset of R contained in [0, infinity)). This is implicit in the paper's notation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))

The nearby motivation is implicit in your draft but explicit in the paper: Theorem 15 already shows that every set A⊂[0, infinity) with 0∈A is C(B) for some B⊂R, but the proof uses transfinite induction and gives no descriptive information about B. Problem 33 asks whether this witness can be chosen Borel when A is Borel. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
refined_question: Let C(X) denote the center of distances of a set X⊂R in the usual metric, that is, C(X)={α≥0: for every x∈X there exists y∈X with |x-y|=α}. Is it true that for every Borel set A⊂[0, infinity) with 0∈A, there exists a Borel set B⊂R such that C(B)=A?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation to your draft. Section 7 defines the operator C, then states Theorem 15 giving the unrestricted existence result, and immediately formulates the Borel version as Problem 33. The paper then highlights Problem 34 as a more specific compact special case, so the exact target captured by your draft is Problem 33 rather than a broader neighboring realization problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.17285))
